title: Non-adjustable time limit
user_impact: Users need more time to enter data and may lose data through timeouts.
technical_impact: Missing refresh or timeout handling in the script/markup.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (20-hour exception); technique H76/F40/F41; HTML 'shared declarative refresh steps'
checks.applicability: meta elements with http-equiv=refresh (any case) whose content starts with digits, also when inserted by script.
checks.expectation:
Fails at the meta element when it reloads or redirects after a delay of
1 s up to just under 20 hours (71999 s fails, 72000 s is the 20-hour
exception and passes): users can neither stop nor extend it. Attribute case,
leading whitespace and a url part do not matter. Content without leading
digits is ignored by browsers and passes. A delay of 0 is an immediate
redirect, not a time limit (H76); it is not exercised in the corpus because
it would navigate the fixture away.
